statement: On the problem-185 test distribution with N<=1000, BnB with greedy coloring bound completes within 1900ms under normal system load, achieving score 100 without needing local search. The iter-1 observed variance (90-100) was caused by system load, not algorithmic timeout.
regime: problem-185 test distribution, N<=1000, M<=500000, normal system load (no heavy background processes)
mechanism: The BnB with greedy coloring bound (solution.cpp:18-80 in iter-2 v4, or expand() in iter-1) explores the search tree efficiently enough to find the optimal clique on all test cases within 1900ms when the system is not under contention. The 1800ms timeout leaves sufficient margin.
applicability_bounds: May not hold under heavy system load — iter-1 showed a score of 90 in one run, likely from load-induced timeout. The local search provides insurance against this failure mode.

statement: Swap-based local search (1-remove/2-add + random perturbation) provides defensive value against BnB timeout but is not necessary for score 100 under normal conditions on the problem-185 test distribution.
regime: problem-185 test distribution, BnB timeout at 1800ms, local search budget 100ms
evidence: iteration-2-h-control-negative: 5/5 runs scored 100 without local search
mechanism: Local search activates only when BnB sets timed_out=true (solution.cpp:308). Under normal load, BnB completes within 1800ms, so local search never runs. Its value is as insurance: when system load causes BnB to timeout, local search can recover using the remaining ~100ms budget.
applicability_bounds: The defensive value becomes critical under system load. The 100ms local search budget is tight — if both BnB and local search are starved for time, scores may still drop.
